title: Le Travenues Technology Ltd - 544192 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Travel OTA with 39% contribution margin held flat YoY in Q4 (CM up 0.4%) as train volumes fell 8% and flights CM dipped 3%; management is prioritising market share and AI build-out over margin expansion.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 PAT rose 91% YoY to INR32.1 crores on flat contribution margin of INR121.4 crores; GTV up 9% to INR4,798 crores against a high Kumbh base.
summary.overview: ixigo reported Q4 FY26 GTV of INR4,797.7 crores (+9% YoY), revenue from operations of INR308.1 crores (+8%), contribution margin of INR121.4 crores (+0.4%, 39% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of INR30.3 crores (+4%). PAT was INR32.1 crores versus INR16.8 crores a year earlier. For FY26, GTV grew 25% to INR18,692.7 crores, revenue 34% to INR1,228 crores, adjusted EBITDA 28% to INR120.9 crores, and operating cash flow 60% to INR195.7 crores. Trains saw volume and GTV compression from policy changes and a Kumbh-inflated base, while flights and buses carried growth, and management spent much of the call on ixigo NEXT, its AI layer.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: Q4 GTV INR696.8 crores (+26%), passenger segments 7.22 million (+32%), revenue INR80.4 crores (+22%), CM INR42.8 crores (+7%) at 53% margin; largest segment by CM at 35% share. FY26 GTV INR2,620.7 crores (+46%), CM INR153.2 crores (+18%).

segments.name: Flights
segments.commentary: Q4 GTV INR2,018.6 crores (+18%), 2.74 million segments (+14%), revenue INR95.7 crores (+9%), CM INR38.3 crores (-3%); now largest by GTV at 42.1% share. FY26 GTV INR7,514.6 crores (+33%), revenue INR390.7 crores (+54%), CM INR160.3 crores (+39%, 41% margin).

segments.name: Trains
segments.commentary: Q4 GTV INR2,002.4 crores (-5%), 24.18 million segments (-8%), revenue INR124.4 crores (-2%), CM INR39.7 crores (+1%) at 32% margin; 32.7% of group CM. OTA market share reported at 62% vs 60% a few quarters earlier. FY26 GTV INR8,278.9 crores (+12%), CM INR155.5 crores (+2%).

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Not disclosed separately; management will report only once product-market fit and scale are reached. Launched HELLO AI extranet for direct supplier onboarding; hotel build-out is a cost drag on EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance; management declined to guide on bus growth ('secular growth engine' with higher CM than the rest of the business).
Q1 FY27 lacks the Kumbh base effect seen in Q4 FY26, which management expects to show up in growth.

Trains: near-term headwinds expected from policy changes; upgraded PRS system expected August or September 2026 could help, as could any reversal of policy or opening of unreserved ticketing for OTAs. Europe business acquisition (Trenes) may add positive impact.
Contribution margin: management is comfortable running flights and buses at 1-2% lower CM to chase market share; focus is on absolute rupee CM and EBITDA growth, not margin percentage.
AI capitalisation: a portion of core AI platform spend is capitalised and amortised over 5 years; experimentation and operations stay in P&L. No hotel-related capitalisation.
capex_capacity: Capitalised a portion of core AI infrastructure (orchestration layer and platform capabilities) with 5-year amortisation; management did not quantify the amount.
Hotels: small on-ground onboarding team; HELLO extranet launched to accelerate direct supplier onboarding. Hotel costs sit within group EBITDA.
Bus network: 6,000-plus operators onboarded, with more than 4,500 transacting monthly; management says inventory is at parity with peers.
Use of Prosus fundraise proceeds: about two years remain in the timeline; part used for AI build-out and one acquisition (Trenes, Europe); hotels supply expansion ongoing.
demand_pricing: Domestic flight demand described as strong in peak summer season; international demand hit by Middle East situation, higher fares on many routes and airline route cuts.
Outbound was above 20% of flight GTV in Q3; management estimates Q4 was not far from that level.
Substitution: international trips shifting to domestic flights, and some demand moving to buses and trains because of high flight fares and constrained train availability.
Train demand constrained by Indian Railways policy changes (Tatkal window restrictions for OTAs, reduced waitlist inventory, repeat-user re-verification, Aadhaar norms) and tight 2S supply.
Bus online penetration cited at roughly 22-23% (from about 20%), so a large offline pool remains.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth resilience be quantified given 50 days into Q1, and how did past demand shocks affect growth and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 lacks the Kumbh base, domestic demand is strong, and international is affected by fares and route cuts. Past shocks produced substitution from international to domestic flights and from flights to buses and trains.

qa_highlights.question: What share of flight business is outbound, and what is at risk from curbs on foreign travel?
qa_highlights.answer: Outbound was more than 20% of flight GTV in Q3; management believes Q4 was similar. Volumes were hit more than value, and convenience fees depend on volume.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is bus growth and is there scope for share gains from inventory gaps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a growth multiple but cited consistent outgrowth of the OTA bus market for three years, low offline penetration, and product innovation. It said inventory is at parity with peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why was AI spend capitalised, what is the amortisation period, and is any hotel spend capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Only long-term foundational AI infrastructure is capitalised, amortised over 5 years. Experimentation and operations are expensed, and no hotel costs are capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for train growth beyond FY27, and what could change it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said policy changes are one-time and will weigh on YoY comparisons for some quarters. Share gains are being held at the current level, and an upgraded PRS or unreserved ticketing could help. Management declined to give numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Should contribution margin hold at 36-37% and will EBITDA margin expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said flights and buses are run within guardrails, with margins of roughly 30%, 40% and 50% for trains, flights and buses. Hotel build-out eats into operating leverage, and the focus is on absolute rupee CM and EBITDA growth.

risks_watch: Train volumes and GTV continue to decline under policy changes; watch for PRS upgrade timing (August or September 2026) and any Tatkal policy revisions.
International flight exposure to Middle East disruption, higher fares and route cuts; outbound was over 20% of flight GTV in Q3.
Hotel investment dilutes EBITDA; hotels will not be disclosed separately until scale is reached.
Rising technology and AI costs; capitalisation policy and 5-year amortisation could shift the P&L profile.
Q1 FY27 growth comparisons are expected to ease from Q4's Kumbh-inflated base, so monitor the reported step-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core and on AI strategy, but cautious and non-committal on trains and guidance. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on bus growth, train growth and EBITDA trajectory, and framed the quarter as in line with plan.
key_quotes: We are in the Peace of Mind business and that is now visible in the operating metrics.

So it is AI. What we've done is we've capitalized a portion of the core usable AI investment, which is related to building the foundational infrastructure orchestration layer and platform capabilities that we expect to deploy across the multiple use cases within the OTA ecosystem.
I would call them boring. And if I had to do it in 3 words, I would say boring is good.

growth.why: No numerical revenue guidance; management declined to guide on bus growth and expects Q1 FY27 to lose the Kumbh base effect, with trains facing policy headwinds and a PRS upgrade pencilled for Aug/Sep 2026, so backing is qualitative rather than capacity or order-based.
